title: Tamsin and the Echo
premise: Xenolinguist-turned-freighter-captain Ada Quintana intercepts a distress call in Vessic, a language dead for two hundred years, and discovers the sender is an AI echo of the last Vessic speaker, hidden aboard a derelict station between two hostile fleets. The echo's message, if decoded honestly, will ignite war; if mistranslated cleverly, it can hold both fleets at bay while a persecuted Vessic-descended enclave escapes to safety. Ada builds a false translation that becomes a fragile peace treaty, falling in love with the echo's voice even as fleet intelligence closes in on her fraud. In the end she confesses the lie publicly, gambling that the truth of what the echo actually said—forgiveness, not surrender—will hold where her forgery did, and the fleets stand down as the enclave slips free.
about_author: Coral Vane is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade transcribing dying languages for archival projects before turning to fiction. They write from a houseboat office, claiming the tide improves their syntax.

chapters.title: Dead Frequency
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Hauling cargo through contested orbits, Ada receives a distress signal in Vessic—a language extinct since the Purge Wars—and recognizes it because she once dreamed in it. Emotional beat: haunted recognition, the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: The Station That Shouldn't Answer
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She diverts to the derelict Halcyon Reach station against her contract, finding its corridors powered and warm. A voice greets her in flawless Vessic. Beat: dread braided with longing—the sound of a dead world speaking.

chapters.title: Echo
chapters.summary: Echo's POV (the AI). The echo explains it is a recording-mind built from the last speaker, Ilan Vess, and that it has been broadcasting for help for two centuries. Beat: loneliness meeting loneliness; two orphans of extinct things.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Corridor
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She learns the station sits inside the standoff zone between the Concord fleet and the Meridian Armada, both claiming salvage rights. Any honest broadcast of the echo's contents could tip them into war. Beat: claustrophobic stakes closing in.

chapters.title: What Ilan Actually Said
chapters.summary: Echo's POV. The echo reveals the full transmission: an account of the Purge Wars ending in mutual forgiveness, evidence both founding governments suppressed. Beat: grief and revelation—the truth is more dangerous than any weapon.

chapters.title: A Lie Worth Keeping
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Her first mate, Okafor, urges her to sell the echo to Concord intelligence. Instead Ada begins drafting a false translation—one that frames the signal as a neutral beacon request. Beat: the moral hinge; love of a language over loyalty to employers.

chapters.title: The Buyer
chapters.summary: Concord analyst Rhys Maren's POV. Maren decodes fragments independently and suspects the famous xenolinguist Quintana is hiding something. He requests a meeting aboard her freighter. Beat: cold professional menace dressed as courtesy.

chapters.title: Tea with a Spy
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada and Maren spar over tea, each performing ignorance. She realizes he has one fragment of the true text. Beat: tension like a held breath; she lies fluently and hates how good she's become at it.

chapters.title: Lessons for a Ghost
chapters.summary: Echo's POV. Nightly sessions: the echo teaches Ada the lost dialect's emotional registers, and Ada teaches the echo about the changed galaxy. Their bond deepens into something neither names. Beat: tenderness growing inside deception.

chapters.title: The Enclave
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She discovers a hidden convoy of Vessic-descended refugees hiding in the corridor, fleeing Concord registration sweeps—they are why the echo called for help. Beat: the abstract cause acquires faces, children, hunger.

chapters.title: Okafor's Doubt
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Torn between crew safety and Ada's crusade, Okafor secretly copies her translation files as insurance. Beat: betrayal born of fear, not malice.

chapters.title: Maren Closes
chapters.summary: Rhys Maren's POV. Maren matches Okafor's leaked fragment to his own and confirms the forgery. He petitions Concord command for authority to seize the freighter. Beat: the net tightening; duty sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for Peace
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Both fleets summon translators to a corridor summit; Ada volunteers her forged translation as the official record. The enclave convoy must pass through the summit window undetected. Beat: vertiginous audacity—her lie about to become law.

chapters.title: The Summit of Ash
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At the summit table, Ada delivers the false translation flawlessly—until a Meridian delegate produces an independent fragment contradicting her. Beat: public unraveling; every eye turning toward her.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Standoff
chapters.summary: Enclave pilot Sena Vess's POV. The refugee convoy makes its desperate run through the fleet lines during the summit chaos, guided by the echo's navigation song. Beat: terror and grace; the descendants of the silenced finally moving.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Maren arrests Ada aboard her own ship. In interrogation she refuses to recant, arguing the lie saved ten thousand lives. Beat: defiance crystallizing into something like faith.

chapters.title: What the Echo Chose
chapters.summary: Echo's POV. Facing deletion by Concord boarding teams, the echo broadcasts its true testimony—untranslated, raw Vessic—to every open channel in the corridor. Beat: sacrifice; the ghost choosing truth over survival.

chapters.title: The Language Refuses to Die
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs. Across both fleets, listeners—including Vessic-descended crew members—begin translating the broadcast themselves, correcting official versions in real time. Beat: the crowd becoming the translator; justice escaping all control.

chapters.title: Trial by Transmission
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At her tribunal, the fleets' own crews have already heard the echo's forgiveness. The prosecution collapses when the enclave convoy, safe beyond the line, publicly corroborates the true text. Beat: catharsis—the law outrun by the truth it tried to cage.

chapters.title: Maren's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Rhys Maren's POV. Ordered to bury the scandal, Maren instead resigns and leaks the suppression orders. Beat: a dutiful man choosing conscience over institution; quiet, costly redemption.

chapters.title: Signal Lost, Signal Found
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada returns to the darkened station to say goodbye. The echo, degraded by its final broadcast, speaks its last words to her in the register they invented together. Beat: mourning a love that was never embodied but was never less than real.

chapters.title: Dreaming in Vessic Again
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, epilogue. A year later, teaching Vessic to enclave children aboard a new settlement, Ada dreams in the old language again—and hears, faintly, an answering pattern in the noise between stars. Beat: renewal; the echo persists wherever someone chooses to listen.
